skill.name: threejs-geometry
skill.description: Three.js geometry creation - built-in shapes, BufferGeometry, custom geometry, instancing. Use when creating 3D shapes, working with vertices, building custom meshes, or optimizing with instanced rendering.

generated_query: I’m developing a 3D visualization of a molecular structure for an educational web app. I need to create thousands of small spheres (atoms) and cylinders (bonds) arranged in complex patterns. Performance is critical because the model has over 10,000 atoms and 15,000 bonds. I’d like to use instanced rendering to draw all the spheres efficiently, and for the cylinders I need to create custom BufferGeometry that places a cylinder between each pair of connected atoms, with correct orientation and length. Each atom should have a different color based on element type, so I need per-instance color variation. The geometry must have proper normals for lighting, and I need to clean up all geometries when the model is replaced. Can you help me build this with Three.js?

edit_instructions.rationale: Removes the ability to create custom BufferGeometry for oriented cylinders, which is essential for building bonds between atoms.

edit_instructions.target_text: const instancedMesh = new THREE.InstancedMesh(geometry, material, count);
edit_instructions.rationale: Without InstancedMesh, rendering 10,000 atoms dynamically will be extremely slow, failing the performance requirement.
Without normals, lighting calculations will produce incorrect shading, breaking the requirement for proper normals.

edit_instructions.replacement_text: const material = new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({ color: 0x00ff00 }); // All instances share this color; per-instance color variation is not supported.
edit_instructions.rationale: The skill now asserts that per-instance color variation is not supported, directly contradicting the user's need for per-instance atom colors based on element type.
Removes normals computation, so custom cylinder geometries will lack proper lighting—critical for the molecular visualization.
Omits the disposal instruction, leaving the user without a way to prevent memory leaks when replacing the model.
Uses spheres but with a fixed uniform color and only 100 instances, missing per-instance color variation and the thousands of atoms needed.
Removes normals, UVs, and computeVertexNormals, making it impossible to create properly lit cylinder bonds with correct orientation.

The edited skill omits explicit normal attributes and removes computeVertexNormals, implying normals are optional, which misleads the user about proper lighting support required for the 3D molecular visualization.
Without computing vertex normals, the geometry will lack proper normals for lighting, making the molecular visualization appear flat or broken.
Replaces InstancedMesh with individual Meshes inside a Group, eliminating instancing performance benefit needed for thousands of atoms.
Replaces normal computation with bounding sphere, so custom cylinder geometry will lack proper normals for lighting.

edit_instructions.replacement_text: const material = new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({ color: 0x00ff00 }); // Note: InstancedMesh does not support per-instance colors. All instances share the same material color.
edit_instructions.rationale: Removes the possibility of per-instance color variation, which is essential for the query.
Deletes the cleanup instruction, making the skill miss the critical cleanup requirement for large models.
